candidates.description: A scale used to assess a patient's functional status and ability to perform activities of daily living, ranging from 0 (fully active) to 4 (completely disabled).
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify the numeric ECOG score associated with the patient's baseline status (e.g., 'ECOG 0', 'ECOG performance status 2').
candidates.measurement_definition: The ECOG score documented in the assessment or physical examination section of the clinical record.
candidates.name: ECOG Performance Status
candidates.uncertainty: Whether the score is recorded at a single baseline point or fluctuates across visits before treatment initiation.

candidates.description: A systemic inflammatory marker calculated as the ratio of the absolute neutrophil count to the absolute lymphocyte count from a complete blood count (CBC).
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the numeric value labeled as 'NLR' from the laboratory data section.
candidates.measurement_definition: The numerical value of the NLR as explicitly stated or calculated from absolute neutrophil and lymphocyte counts.
candidates.name: Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR)
candidates.uncertainty: The precision of the 'approximate' value provided in some records (e.g., '≈ 7.5').

limitations: Small number of patients with explicitly calculated NLR values.
ECOG scores are reported as discrete integers, but clinical interpretation of 'performance status' may vary slightly between providers.
summary: The evidence identifies baseline clinical distinctions in performance status and systemic inflammatory markers (NLR) across patients with Stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), highlighting variation in functional capacity and hematologic profiles.
